6.0.0.en: Christ speaks here about the basic pillars of worship, which are almsgiving, prayer and fasting. Perhaps He begins with almsgiving as an extension of His previous words about offering love and doing good to everyone, even enemies. And He sets a basic condition for the acceptance of almsgiving, which is that it be for God's sake, and not with the aim that people should see us and glorify us, because if we receive the praise of people, we have no reward with God. In ancient times the hypocrites did not give alms because of their love for God and for the needy, but gave alms for their personal glory, so they sounded trumpets so that people would gather and see the greatness of their giving and glorify them.

6.0.1.en: "Your Father which is in heaven": he means God, who is exalted above the earthly, passing thoughts of the hypocrites, and with whom we prepare to be in eternal life, and receive the reward of our righteous life on earth in the eternal heavenly inheritance.

6.0.2.en: "Hypocrites": those who show what is different from what they hold within; their appearance is the work of mercy, and their reality is pride and seeking the praise of people; and what is meant here is the scribes and Pharisees.

6.0.3.en: "In the synagogues and in the streets": where people are numerous, so that they may offer them greater praise.

6.1.0.en: The left hand: it signifies giving to win the praise of people.

6.1.1.en: The right hand: it signifies blessing and obedience to the commandment, that is, giving for God's sake. He also means that giving should be in secret, so that it is hidden even from those nearest to us, like the nearness of one hand to the other; then almsgiving is for God's sake alone, and we receive the eternal reward, which will be before all creation, and God also blesses us in our earthly life before all.

6.1.2.en: This does not mean that a person should not give if there is someone who sees him, for we do not withhold giving because it cannot be hidden, but let us have the spirit of secrecy, and not be occupied with the opinion of people.

6.1.3.en: Care for the needy who cannot ask openly, for these who are concealed may be more in need than all, and thank God who permitted you to give to Him in the form of these needy ones.

6.2.0.en: Christ did not tell us the details of individual or communal prayer, but left these details to the Church, to arrange by His Holy Spirit.

6.2.1.en: He spoke of the essence of prayer, that it be a personal bond of love between man and God. How, then, do you put it on display before people to receive their glory, whether in crowded places like the synagogues where the assembled see you, or in the corners of the streets so that those coming from the different streets see you? In this you will receive the glory of people, and lose the eternal reward.

6.2.2.en: Therefore the children of God should pray in secret, and shut the doors so that no one sees them. What is meant is the doors of the heart before the material doors, because if a person enters his closet, and his heart wishes that people know that he is inside praying so that they may glorify him, he will not receive God's blessing. This does not mean that a person should be troubled if someone sees him while he prays, whether in his own room or in the church or in any place, but what matters is that his heart not desire that people see him and glorify him.

6.3.0.en: In ancient times some, in pagan worship and then among the Jews, used to read prayers and repeat them many times, thinking that by much repetition the prayer is answered; this is vain repetition which benefits nothing. But sound repetition is persistence with God in supplication and faith, that is, the person understands what he says, and it is not merely the repetition of the lips.

6.3.1.en: And Christ affirms that God knows our needs, so repetition is of no use, as though God did not hear. All that He awaits from us is to turn to Him and open our hearts to Him. When we show our sonship and our clinging to Him, He pours out His mercies upon us; God awaits our asking, because He loves us, and knows our need, and wishes to give to us if we love Him and ask Him. If you are occupied during prayer with people's opinion of you, and they approve of your words, you have received your reward on earth, and this prayer profits you nothing before God. So open your heart in your own room, or away from eyes, to express all your feelings in words and tears and prostration, and your heart is comforted by the grace of God, who hears you and rejoices in your prayer.

6.4.0.en: Christ Himself gave us the example that we follow in all our prayers, which is the Lord's Prayer, which we recite often before, during and at the end of our prayers.

6.4.1.en: The Lord's Prayer includes three petitions for the glorification of God's name, which are petitions of love for His person and extend to find their fulfillment in eternity, then three other petitions for our material needs, to teach us to honor God and glorify Him before asking anything for ourselves.

6.4.2.en: "Our Father": this prayer begins by showing our special sonship to God, so we enter prayer with this boldness, and this Father of ours is exalted above all sin, so if we are His children, we walk in purity as heavenly beings while we are on earth. He is not exalted in the visible heaven, but dwells in our hearts, which are purified by repentance and by His love, and so become a heaven. "Hallowed be thy name": God's name means all of God, for a person's name indicates all that is in him. We do not ask for God's holiness because He is holy in Himself, but for His being hallowed in our sight and in our life, that is, that our hearts be pure and consecrated to Him, so that they are fit for His dwelling, so we reject all evil by repentance, and prepare our hearts for prayers, meditations and every good work.

6.5.0.en: "Thy kingdom come": God is the owner of everything in the world, but we ask that He reign over our hearts, so that we may enjoy His fatherhood, care and love. In this we drive out every sin that has control over us, and every earthly attachment. It also means our longing for the heavenly Kingdom in eternity, where God reigns without hindrance over our hearts and completes our joy.

6.5.1.en: "Thy will be done": we, as children of God, ask for His will and not our will, because our will is liable to error, but His will is always good for our benefit. And He, in His fatherhood, seeks our good and our arrival at His blessed eternity. "In earth, as it is in heaven": the angels in heaven submit to God, and we wish to obey His word on earth as they obey Him in heaven, for there the conflict between body and spirit ceases, and a person lives in constant enjoyment of God. Therefore we wish that our earthly life be turned into a heavenly life, in which the body agrees with the spirit in the love of God and service of Him.

6.5.2.en: Heaven also signifies holiness, so as the saints live seeking God's will, we also wish to be like them.

6.5.3.en: And heaven points spiritually to faith, where the faithful are happy with life with God; so we ask that all the earth believe in God and become a heaven.

6.6.0.en: "Our daily bread": it is sometimes translated "our bread for tomorrow" or "our coming bread" or "our essential bread".

6.6.1.en: "Daily" (sufficient): the bread that suffices us today, and we are not anxious or occupied with the future.

6.6.2.en: Our bread for tomorrow or the coming bread: that is, the heavenly spiritual food, which we need to taste from now on earth.

6.6.3.en: Essential: that is, the spiritual food, which is the most important, to distinguish it from the passing material food.

6.6.4.en: All these translations mean one spiritual idea, which is: give us our necessary bread, that is:

6.6.5.en: (1) Our necessary material needs that suffice us today, and we do not care about tomorrow since we trust in Your care, and that You will always supply our needs, so our heart is occupied with soaring in Your love.

6.6.6.en: (2) The word of God through the Holy Bible, and prayer and the Midnight Praise (Tasbeha), for they satisfy us more than material food.

6.6.7.en: (3) Partaking of the Holy Mysteries, whether by partaking daily, or by feeling it if we partake at longer intervals (weekly, for example).

6.6.8.en: We learn from all the preceding meanings, whether the material bread whose sweetness we feel because it is God's heavenly gift to us, or the sense of Christ with us daily through the means of grace and the Holy Sacraments, that all these are a pledge of the Kingdom which we taste on earth so that we long for heaven.

6.7.0.en: The petition for forgiveness of sin is a clear confession that we are sinners offering repentance before God, confident of His forgiveness and His love that does not reject us.

6.7.1.en: It also means our weakness and constant need for forgiveness, because, although our nature was renewed in Baptism, we are liable to fall into sin every day, so we receive forgiveness in the prayer of repentance and the sacrament of confession. The Lord's Prayer sets a condition for obtaining forgiveness, which is love for others and forbearance and forgiving their sins, because it is unreasonable for the hard-hearted, unforgiving person, who is a judge of others, to obtain forgiveness from God. If God is ready to forgive our sins against Him, which are unlimited sins since He is unlimited, then all the more should we forgive our brethren their sins against us, because they are limited sins, since we are limited. So when you forgive another you gain the greater thing, which is God's forgiveness of your unlimited sins. And this forgiveness of yours to your brother purifies your heart so that you are worthy of God's forgiveness, but he needs to repent in order to obtain God's forgiveness.

6.8.0.en: "Lead us not into temptation": a phrase that means a person's humility and his feeling of his weakness, so he asks God to keep temptations away from him. But if God's will allows a person to pass through a temptation, let him ask God, saying: "But deliver us from evil": that is, do not allow the devil to dominate us, and do not forsake us so that we fall into temptation, but with Your help we endure it and come out of it pure, and even increase in virtue. For real temptation is not merely tribulation, but falling into sin and departing from God, and this is what we ask God to protect us from. Then He concludes the Lord's Prayer with the glorification of God, confessing, saying: "For thine is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, for ever. Amen."

6.8.1.en: "The kingdom": that is, He reigns over the heart as was asked previously.

6.8.2.en: "The power": a confession of God's power that is able to answer our prayer.

6.8.3.en: "The glory": He is worthy of glorification and honor at all times.

6.8.4.en: And this confession means submission to God, not by the lips only, but by deed as well.

6.8.5.en: The last three petitions concern our life on earth, because in heaven we do not need material food, or a pledge of the Kingdom, because we will have reached it, and there is no sin, so we do not need forgiveness, and there is no temptation or Satan to fear.

6.9.0.en: Because of the importance of loving others, God repeats the necessity of forgiving them and being forbearing with them, otherwise we lose all the blessings of the Lord's Prayer and God's love for us.

6.9.1.en: And because of its importance, He repeats it twice in these two verses.

6.9.2.en: May you be aware of the meanings of this prayer when you recite it every day, so that you enter into God's presence with the boldness of sonship and seek His glory, and declare your longing for Him. Then, with the need of a son, ask all that you want, confident of His love.

6.10.0.en: "When ye fast": just as almsgiving and prayer are necessary, so also is fasting.

6.10.1.en: And He speaks here about its manner, while the arrangement of communal fasts He left to the Apostles and the holy Fathers in the first generations.

6.10.2.en: "Of a sad countenance": the scribes and Pharisees, when they fasted, did not wash their faces, and put ashes on their heads so as to appear fasting before people, and so receive their praise.

6.10.3.en: "They have their reward": that is, their fasting is worthless before God.

6.11.0.en: On the contrary, Christ showed the importance of hiding the fast, because it is a personal bond of love between man and God, for he leaves something for His sake. Therefore He asked that the person's appearance be ordinary, not sad, that is, his face washed and his hair anointed.

6.11.1.en: And from the spiritual side, washing the face signifies purity from sin by repentance, and anointing the hair signifies joy in fellowship with God and in the spiritual practices during the fast.

6.12.0.en: He affirms here the importance of the divine reward for those who fast, with blessings on earth, then eternal life, as happens with those who pray and give alms.

6.12.1.en: And if your grumbling appears over the fast or any spiritual worship, you have lost your heavenly reward. So take care to hide your fast as much as you can, because it is a bond of love between you and God. But if someone knows that you are fasting, do not be troubled, because you did not seek that.

6.13.0.en: Christ warns us against placing our hope in earthly things, so that we fall into the love of possessing, because all possessions are exposed to corruption, either by insects and rust and the forces of time, or they are exposed to theft by robbers, so they are changeable and passing; how then can a person's hope be changeable and passing?! And on the other, positive side He calls us to have our treasures in heaven, far from any change or passing away, and that by exerting effort in holy worship and works of mercy.

6.13.1.en: This does not mean that saving and providing for a person's needs and various projects is regarded as wrong, but the wrong is in the heart's attachment to money and relying on it.

6.14.0.en: The place where you lay up treasure indicates the desire of your heart and your preoccupation; if your treasure is heavenly, your heart is directed toward heaven, and consequently your heart moves you to grow and become spiritually strong, and reach the Kingdom. And the opposite, if you are earthly, that is, your treasures are on earth, your end is perdition.

6.14.1.en: Overcome material things and their changes so that you do not rely on them, and so use them without attachment, content with what you have, whether much or little, giving thanks at all times for God's gifts, confident that what you have is your suitable need which God sent you. And if you want something else, ask Him, but with reliance and acceptance of His will; that is, if He sends it to you, thank Him, and if He does not send it, thank Him also, enjoying what is more important, which is your love for Him.

6.15.0.en: By the eye He means not only the outward eye but also the inward, that is, the heart. If it is single, that is, sees things as they are, as God sees them, and does not see evil, that is, sees all that is good, and does not seek excuses for faults and keeps away from them, then the body, that is, the works, becomes full of light, that is, good.

6.16.0.en: If we look at faults in order to condemn them, we are exposed to falling, and thus our works are wrong, that is, dark. The eye is the entrance of good things into the body, that is, it is what sees God in the things around it, and so leads the body to works of good. But if the eye itself is evil, it will bring new evils into the person, and his sins become very ugly.

6.16.1.en: Ask yourself how Christ would look at matters if He were in your place, so that you can see them as they truly are without personal aims or wrong thoughts, and do not mislead yourself.

6.16.2.en: Seek everything good in what is around you and thank God for it, and if you see faults in others, pray for them that God may set right what is in them and make up their shortcomings, and thus you see only God in those around you, whether good, which is from Him, or evil, which He sets right.

6.17.0.en: By money here He means all the possessions in the world, of food and clothing and anything material that we use and buy with money.

6.17.1.en: And although money is a blessing from God, attachment to it makes us enslaved to it, and we are separated from the worship of God. It is impossible to combine the two loves, so either we love God, or we love the world and the material things in it. When we love God, we use all our energies for the glory of His name, but if we love money, our whole life is directed to gathering it and delighting in it.

6.18.0.en: God shows us the importance of life with Him, so that we do not lose our life and direct it to acquiring food and clothing, but on the contrary, we are content with the least possible of them, to be free for life with God and to enjoy it in His hands, offering proof of this, which is that our life itself is better than these passing material things. And God, who gave us this life and this body, is of course able to give us what is less important, which is its needs.

6.19.0.en: God calls us to rely on Him, and offers a second proof, which is looking at the birds of the air, which fly off singing His praise, without worrying about their bodily needs and storing for the future, for God feeds them day by day.

6.19.1.en: And of course man, the head of creation, is cared for by God, who gives him his needs if he relies on Him.

6.19.2.en: Then He offers a third proof, which is: what have those concerned with material things gained, have they been able to add one cubit to their stature (about 50 cm)? For God is the one who gives the length of the body and its form, and preserves it if we rely on Him.

6.20.0.en: God gives us a fourth proof calling us to rely on Him, which is meditating on the lilies of the field, that is, the various kinds of flowers that have very beautiful forms, which man tries to imitate in the shapes of his clothes, but does not reach their beauty, for Solomon the king, despite his greatness and abundance of money, his clothes did not reach the beauty of these flowers, though they are merely grasses that grow for a few months and then wither and are burned with fire in the oven. So what is the value of man in God's sight? ... It is far greater, and God cares to clothe him and supply his needs. If he believes in God, however few his resources or works, God will provide his needs, as He gives beauty to the flowers that cannot dig or spin, so He gives them an embroidered beautiful appearance, better than all the garments spun by human hands.

6.21.0.en: In conclusion, do not be anxious about your material needs as the rest of mankind does, but be assured that God, your heavenly Father, knows your needs and will provide them for you, and care only to seek that God reign over your hearts and that you enjoy fellowship with Him, confident that the rest of the matters are very easy for God to provide for you, better than you providing them by your much preoccupation; though we must carry out our duties and not be lazy.

6.22.0.en: It is concluded from this that we should do our daily duties, and not be occupied with the future and its troubles (that is, its evil), so that the heart is free to enjoy God today, and He will arrange tomorrow.

6.22.1.en: See how much time you spend caring for material things, and how much time you are occupied with being with God? Do not forget that your goal is God, so arrange your day so that God is the priority, indeed in everything you do, see that it is pleasing to God, and likewise your words and thoughts.

6.22.2.en: And let you have spiritual ambition and constructive thoughts, confident of God's provision for your needs and His protection of you. The Sermon on the Mount continued; Not judging; Acting on the commandment
